timeline.event: Villagers at 'Ain Ghazal model large lime-plaster human statues
timeline.label: c. 6500 BCE

timeline.event: King Mesha of Moab sets up his victory stele at Dhiban
timeline.label: c. 840 BCE

timeline.event: Rome annexes the Nabataean kingdom and its capital Petra
Jerash builds a triumphal arch for Emperor Hadrian's visit
The Madaba mosaic map of the Holy Land is laid in a church floor
timeline.label: c. 560

timeline.event: Arab Muslim armies defeat the Byzantines at the Yarmouk River
Crusaders begin building Kerak Castle
The Ottoman Empire takes control of the region
Johann Ludwig Burckhardt reaches Petra in disguise
Circassian settlers refound Amman among its Roman ruins
The Hejaz Railway reaches Medina
Sharif Hussein of Mecca launches the Arab Revolt
Abdullah founds the Emirate of Transjordan
Transjordan becomes independent and Abdullah is proclaimed king
King Talal issues the constitution still in force today
Jordan is admitted to the United Nations
Jordan and Israel sign a peace treaty at Wadi Araba
Abdullah II becomes king after the death of King Hussein
Petra is voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World
Wadi Rum is inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site

places.name: Amman
places.clue: Jordan's hilly capital grew around the citadel of ancient Rabbath Ammon, later the Roman city of Philadelphia.

places.name: Petra
places.clue: The Nabataean capital, carved from rose-red sandstone, was voted one of the New Seven Wonders of the World in 2007.

places.name: Wadi Rum
places.clue: A desert of red sand and sandstone peaks that has stood in for Mars and other alien worlds in Hollywood films.

places.name: Dead Sea
places.clue: At about 430 m below sea level, its shore is the lowest dry land on Earth, and its salty water keeps bathers afloat.

places.name: Aqaba
places.clue: Jordan's only seaport sits on the Red Sea's Gulf of Aqaba, with coral reefs just offshore.

places.name: Kerak Castle
places.clue: Begun by the Crusaders in the 1140s, this hilltop fortress surrendered to Saladin's forces in 1188.

places.name: Umm Qais
places.clue: Ancient Gadara, a Decapolis city built of black basalt, overlooks the Sea of Galilee and the Yarmouk gorge.

places.name: Azraq Wetland Reserve
places.clue: A rare oasis in the eastern desert whose pools and marshes are a vital stopover for migrating birds.

places.name: Umm el-Jimal
places.clue: A town of black basalt houses, churches and reservoirs from Roman to early Islamic times, listed by UNESCO in 2024.

places.name: Qasr Burqu'
places.clue: A remote fort beside a desert lake in the far north-east, expanded in Umayyad times around an older tower.

places.name: Qasr al-Tuba
places.clue: The most remote of the Umayyad desert palaces, a vast brick complex left unfinished in the 8th century.

places.name: Al-Mudawwara
places.clue: A Hejaz Railway station near the Saudi border, raided by Lawrence and Arab forces during the First World War.
